words.enDefinition: A situation in which market choices do not lead to an efficient allocation of resources.

examples.en: The class identified a market failure when the factory's prices ignored costs borne by nearby residents.
examples.zh: 工厂的售价忽略了附近居民承担的成本，全班把这一情形识别为「市场失灵」。

examples.en: Our tutor used the flood warning example to show why market failure can leave services underprovided.
examples.zh: 老师用洪水预警例子说明，「市场失灵」为什么可能导致服务供给不足。

collocations: explain the source of market failure

words.enDefinition: Resource allocation that leaves potential net benefits unrealized by producing too much or too little of something.

examples.en: The tutor illustrated allocative inefficiency by showing that extra units cost society more than they benefited it.
examples.zh: 老师指出，多生产的部分产品给社会带来的成本高于收益，以此解释「配置无效率」。

examples.en: We identified allocative inefficiency where additional workshop places would have produced benefits greater than their costs.
examples.zh: 增加工作坊名额本可带来超过成本的收益，我们在此处识别出「配置无效率」。

collocations: reduce allocative inefficiency in a model

words.enDefinition: The quantity that maximizes net social benefits, where marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost at an interior optimum.

examples.en: We found the socially efficient quantity where marginal social benefit and marginal social cost crossed.
examples.zh: 我们在边际社会收益和边际社会成本相交处找到「社会有效数量」。

examples.en: The market produced more than the socially efficient quantity after ignoring the cost of nearby noise.
examples.zh: 市场忽略了给周边造成的噪声成本，产量因此超过「社会有效数量」。

collocations: compare market output with the socially efficient quantity

words.enDefinition: an effect on others that the decision-maker does not bear or receive through the prices and payments attached to the activity

examples.en: The class identified an externality when noise from deliveries disturbed people who were not buying anything.
examples.zh: 配送发出的噪声打扰了没有购买商品的人，全班把它识别为「外部性」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked which externality might result from planting trees near the shared campus path.
examples.zh: 练习表问，在校园公共小径旁种树可能产生哪种「外部性」。

words.enDefinition: An uncompensated cost imposed on others who are not directly involved in the activity.

examples.en: The example treated delivery noise as a negative externality because it disturbed nearby residents at night.
examples.zh: 例题把配送噪声视为「负外部性」，因为它夜间打扰了附近居民。

examples.en: We discussed a negative externality from litter that remained after customers took their food away.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了顾客带走食物后留下的垃圾所造成的一种「负外部性」。

words.enDefinition: An uncompensated benefit that an activity creates for others outside the relevant decision or transaction.

examples.en: The example showed a positive externality when a workshop shared a design that neighbouring groups could use.
examples.zh: 工作坊分享了邻近小组可以使用的设计，例题展示了由此产生的「正外部性」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked who received the positive externality from caring for trees beside the campus path.
examples.zh: 老师问，养护校园小径旁的树所产生的「正外部性」惠及了谁。

words.enDefinition: An outside benefit or cost created by producing a good or service.

examples.en: The model treated factory noise as a production externality affecting people in the surrounding area.
examples.zh: 模型把工厂噪声看作影响周边居民的「生产外部性」。

examples.en: We compared two processes to see whether either created a production externality in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两种工艺，看其中是否有一种在课堂案例中产生了「生产外部性」。

collocations: estimate the effect of a production externality

words.enDefinition: A benefit or cost that one person's use of a good creates for others.

examples.en: The class discussed a consumption externality when loud outdoor speakers disturbed people studying nearby.
examples.zh: 在室外大声播放的扬声器打扰附近学习者时，全班讨论了由此产生的「消费外部性」。

examples.en: Our example treated benefits to nearby gardens from household composting as a possible consumption externality.
examples.zh: 例题将家庭堆肥给周边花园带来的收益视为一种可能的「消费外部性」。

words.enDefinition: A cost of an activity borne by people other than the decision-makers or parties to the transaction.

examples.en: The worksheet included an external cost for the extra cleaning needed in the streets around the festival.
examples.zh: 练习表计入了节庆周边街道需要额外清洁所产生的一项「外部成本」。

examples.en: We added the external cost to the producer's own cost when comparing the two activities.
examples.zh: 比较两项活动时，我们把「外部成本」加到了生产者自行承担的成本上。

collocations: an external cost borne by residents

words.enDefinition: A benefit of an activity received by people outside the decision or transaction that created it.

examples.en: The case counted an external benefit when shade from a restored garden cooled the neighbouring walkway.
examples.zh: 修复后的花园为邻近步道遮阳降温，案例把这计作一项「外部收益」。

examples.en: Our tutor separated the external benefit from the benefit received by people who attended the workshop.
examples.zh: 老师把「外部收益」和工作坊参加者自身获得的收益分开。

collocations: an external benefit to nearby households

words.enDefinition: The extra cost that a decision-maker bears from producing or undertaking one more unit.

examples.en: The marginal private cost included the materials and labour needed to make one more sample basket.
examples.zh: 「边际私人成本」包括多做一个样品篮子所需的材料和人工。

examples.en: We compared marginal private cost with the additional cost that the same unit imposed on neighbours.
examples.zh: 我们将「边际私人成本」与这一个单位给邻居带来的额外成本作比较。

collocations: draw the marginal private cost curve
compare marginal private cost with marginal social cost

words.enDefinition: The additional cost imposed on third parties by one more unit of an activity.

examples.en: The model's marginal external cost was higher for a delivery on the busy street during quiet hours.
examples.zh: 模型中，同样在繁忙街道上配送，若赶上居民休息时段，「边际外部成本」会更高。

examples.en: We estimated marginal external cost for one additional trip before calculating the corresponding social cost.
examples.zh: 我们先估算多一次出行的「边际外部成本」，再计算对应的社会成本。

collocations: plot the marginal external cost curve
include marginal external cost in the calculation

words.enDefinition: The total extra cost to everyone from one more unit, including private and external costs.

examples.en: We added the firm's extra expense and the neighbours' extra damage to obtain marginal social cost.
examples.zh: 我们将企业多付的费用与邻居额外承受的损害相加，得到「边际社会成本」。

examples.en: The graph placed marginal social cost above marginal private cost because extra production created noise.
examples.zh: 图上的「边际社会成本」高于边际私人成本，因为额外生产会产生噪声。

collocations: draw the marginal social cost curve
compare marginal social cost with the benefit of another unit

words.enDefinition: The additional benefit a decision-maker receives from consuming or undertaking one more unit.

examples.en: The marginal private benefit was the extra value a participant received from attending one more session.
examples.zh: 「边际私人收益」是参加者多参加一场活动所获得的额外价值。

examples.en: Our tutor measured marginal private benefit before counting any benefits received by people outside the workshop.
examples.zh: 老师先测量「边际私人收益」，再计入工作坊之外的人所获得的收益。

collocations: draw the marginal private benefit curve
compare marginal private benefit with marginal social benefit

words.enDefinition: The additional benefit received by third parties when one more unit of an activity takes place.

examples.en: The exercise estimated marginal external benefit from the extra shade one more tree provided to neighbouring houses.
examples.zh: 练习估算了再种一棵树为周边住宅增加树荫所带来的「边际外部收益」。

examples.en: We counted the marginal external benefit separately from the extra benefit enjoyed by the person planting the tree.
examples.zh: 我们把「边际外部收益」与种树人自己获得的额外收益分开计算。

collocations: include marginal external benefit in a welfare comparison

words.enDefinition: The total extra benefit to everyone from one more unit, including private and external benefits.

examples.en: The worksheet added the participant's extra benefit to the spillover to calculate marginal social benefit.
examples.zh: 练习表把参加者的额外收益和外溢收益相加，计算「边际社会收益」。

examples.en: We compared marginal social benefit with marginal social cost for one additional workshop place.
examples.zh: 我们比较了增加一个工作坊名额的「边际社会收益」和边际社会成本。

collocations: plot the marginal social benefit curve
compare marginal social benefit with marginal social cost

words.enDefinition: To make a decision-maker face the outside costs or benefits created by their choices.

examples.en: The class asked whether a fee could internalise an externality created by extra traffic near campus.
examples.zh: 全班讨论收费能否「将外部性内部化」，这里的外部性来自校园附近新增的车流。

examples.en: Our worksheet compared two ways to internalise an externality from noise near the practice factory.
examples.zh: 练习表比较了两种将示例工厂周边噪声的「外部性内部化」的方法。

collocations: internalise an externality through a price
a policy designed to internalise an externality

words.enDefinition: In an externality model, production beyond the quantity that maximizes net social benefits.

examples.en: The model predicted overproduction because sellers did not face the damage caused by each extra unit.
examples.zh: 卖家无需承担每增加一个单位所造成的损害，模型因此预测会有「过度生产」。

examples.en: We marked the range of overproduction between the market quantity and the socially efficient quantity.
examples.zh: 我们在市场数量和社会有效数量之间标出了「过度生产」的范围。

collocations: overproduction caused by an external cost

words.enDefinition: In an externality model, production below the quantity that maximizes net social benefits.

examples.en: The model showed underproduction because sellers could not capture the benefits their activity brought to neighbours.
examples.zh: 卖家无法获得活动为邻居带来的收益，因此模型显示出现「生产不足」。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed underproduction after comparing the number of training places offered with the efficient quantity.
examples.zh: 老师比较实际提供的培训名额与有效数量后，讨论了「生产不足」。

words.enDefinition: A corrective tax that prices a negative externality, set at marginal external cost at the efficient quantity in the benchmark model.

examples.en: The tutor drew a Pigouvian tax equal to the marginal external cost at the efficient quantity.
examples.zh: 老师画出一项「庇古税」，其额度等于有效数量处的边际外部成本。

examples.en: We compared a Pigouvian tax with a classroom rule that simply limited the amount of pollution.
examples.zh: 我们把「庇古税」与课堂模型中直接限制排放量的规定作了比较。

collocations: compare a Pigouvian tax with a cap

words.enDefinition: A subsidy intended to encourage an activity with external benefits by making some of those benefits privately valuable.

examples.en: The worksheet applied a corrective subsidy to reflect the extra benefits one more training place created for others.
examples.zh: 练习表采用「矫正性补贴」，将增加一个培训名额给他人带来的额外收益纳入考虑。

examples.en: Our class set the corrective subsidy equal to the marginal external benefit at the efficient quantity.
examples.zh: 我们全班把「矫正性补贴」设为有效数量下的边际外部收益。

collocations: a corrective subsidy for a positive externality

words.enDefinition: A rule setting a requirement that an activity, product or process must meet.

examples.en: The classroom case compared a regulatory standard for noise with a fee based on the level of noise.
examples.zh: 课堂案例比较了噪声「监管标准」和按噪声水平收取的费用。

examples.en: We asked whether the regulatory standard in the model applied to output or to the production process.
examples.zh: 我们问，模型中的「监管标准」是针对产品还是针对生产过程。

collocations: compare a regulatory standard with a market incentive

words.enDefinition: Direct regulation that sets binding limits or requires specified practices.

examples.en: The case illustrated command-and-control regulation using the same emissions limit for every plant in the model.
examples.zh: 案例在模型中为每家工厂设相同的排放上限，以说明「命令与控制型监管」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what costs firms might face under command-and-control regulation compared with a permit market.
examples.zh: 老师问，与配额市场相比，企业在「命令与控制型监管」下可能面临哪些成本。

words.enDefinition: A regulatory requirement specifying an outcome to meet while leaving some choice over how to meet it.

examples.en: The simulated performance standard set a noise limit while letting workshops choose how to meet it.
examples.zh: 模拟中的「绩效标准」设定噪声限值，同时允许工场自行选择达标方法。

examples.en: We compared a performance standard with a rule that required every firm to install identical equipment.
examples.zh: 我们把「绩效标准」与要求每家企业安装同一种设备的规定作了比较。

collocations: set a performance standard for emissions

words.enDefinition: A regulatory requirement specifying equipment, methods or a type of technology that must be used.

examples.en: The classroom technology standard required each simulated plant to use the same kind of filter.
examples.zh: 课堂模型的「技术标准」要求每家模拟工厂使用同类过滤装置。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether a technology standard left firms room to choose a different production method.
examples.zh: 老师问，「技术标准」是否给企业留下选择其他生产方式的空间。

collocations: compare a technology standard with an outcome-based rule

words.enDefinition: Action that prevents or reduces the amount of pollution generated or released.

examples.en: The model compared pollution abatement at two factories facing the same financial incentive to reduce releases.
examples.zh: 模型比较了两家面对同样减排激励的工厂采取的「污染减排」。

examples.en: Our group measured pollution abatement relative to the level the simulation would have produced without controls.
examples.zh: 我们组以模拟中未设置管控时的排放量为参照，测量了「污染减排」量。

collocations: measure the cost of pollution abatement

words.enDefinition: The additional cost of reducing pollution by one more unit.

examples.en: We compared marginal abatement cost across two factories before explaining who reduced more emissions in the simulation.
examples.zh: 解释模拟中谁减排更多之前，我们比较了两家工厂的「边际减排成本」。

examples.en: The graph showed marginal abatement cost rising as the least expensive reductions were used first.
examples.zh: 图上显示，最便宜的减排措施先用完后，「边际减排成本」会上升。

collocations: draw a marginal abatement cost curve
compare marginal abatement costs across firms

words.enDefinition: The full resource cost of achieving a specified reduction in pollution.

examples.en: The model compared total abatement cost under two policies that achieved the same overall emissions reduction.
examples.zh: 模型比较了两个实现相同总体减排量的政策各自的「减排总成本」。

examples.en: We added each factory's reduction costs to calculate total abatement cost for the entire exercise.
examples.zh: 我们把各工厂的减排成本相加，计算整个练习中的「减排总成本」。

collocations: minimize total abatement cost for a given target

words.enDefinition: A charge based on the amount of pollution an activity releases.

examples.en: The example applied an emissions charge to each unit that the simulated factories continued to release.
examples.zh: 例题对模拟工厂继续排放的每个单位实行「排放收费」。

examples.en: We compared an emissions charge with a rule that put a fixed limit on every factory.
examples.zh: 我们把「排放收费」与对每家工厂都设定固定上限的规定作了比较。

collocations: compare an emissions charge with a permit price

words.enDefinition: Under clear property rights and negligible transaction costs, bargaining can reach an efficient outcome despite an externality.

examples.en: Our tutor introduced the Coase theorem using a case where two neighbours could negotiate at no cost.
examples.zh: 老师用两个邻居可以零成本协商的案例介绍了「科斯定理」。

examples.en: The class discussed why the Coase theorem was harder to apply when many households were affected.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了为什么许多住户受到影响时更难应用「科斯定理」。

collocations: discuss limits of the Coase theorem

words.enDefinition: Clear rules specifying who may use, control, or transfer a resource.

examples.en: The worksheet assumed well-defined property rights before asking how neighbours might negotiate over access to the path.
examples.zh: 练习表先假定存在「明确界定的产权」，再问邻居如何就小径的使用协商。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why well-defined property rights made the parties' starting positions clearer in the example.
examples.zh: 老师解释了为什么例题中「明确界定的产权」使各方的初始立场更清楚。

words.enDefinition: Negotiation between affected parties to agree how to address a cost, benefit or shared concern.

examples.en: The example used private bargaining to show how two neighbours could agree on quieter delivery times.
examples.zh: 例题用「私人协商」展示两个邻居如何就噪声较少的送货时间达成一致。

examples.en: Our class compared private bargaining in a two-person example with a case involving an entire neighbourhood.
examples.zh: 全班对比了两人例题里的「私人协商」和涉及整个街区的案例。

collocations: reach an agreement through private bargaining

words.enDefinition: The time, effort and other resources required to negotiate and carry out an agreement.

examples.en: The case showed high bargaining costs because each household had to coordinate with many other residents.
examples.zh: 每户都要和很多其他居民协调，案例因此显示较高的「协商成本」。

examples.en: We discussed whether bargaining costs included the time needed to find every affected party.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「协商成本」是否包括寻找所有受影响各方所需的时间。

collocations: a model with negligible bargaining costs

words.enDefinition: The emissions level that balances marginal damage and marginal abatement cost at an interior social optimum.

examples.en: We located the socially efficient emissions level where the marginal damage and marginal abatement cost curves met.
examples.zh: 我们在边际损害曲线和边际减排成本曲线相交处找到「社会有效排放水平」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why the socially efficient emissions level in the example was greater than zero.
examples.zh: 老师问，例题中的「社会有效排放水平」为什么大于零。

collocations: calculate the socially efficient emissions level
locate the socially efficient emissions level
compare actual emissions with the socially efficient emissions level

words.enDefinition: A policy tool using prices or tradable rights to change incentives rather than prescribing every action.

examples.en: The worksheet used a market-based instrument to let firms choose how to reduce their own emissions.
examples.zh: 练习表用「市场型政策工具」，让企业自行选择怎样减少本企业的排放。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a market-based instrument with a fixed rule applying to all the simulated firms.
examples.zh: 老师把「市场型政策工具」和适用于所有模拟企业的一条固定规则作了比较。

collocations: choose a market-based instrument for a policy model

words.enDefinition: A transferable authorization to emit a specified amount under an emissions trading system.

examples.en: One factory sold a tradable emissions permit after reducing releases below its allocation in the classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 课堂模拟中，一家工厂将排放降至分配额度以下后，卖出了一份「可交易排放配额」。

examples.en: Our tutor used a tradable emissions permit to explain how a market price could reward lower emissions.
examples.zh: 老师用「可交易排放配额」解释市场价格怎样激励减少排放。

words.enDefinition: A policy that limits aggregate emissions through allowances that participants may trade.
acceptedZhAnswers: 排放总量控制与交易制度

examples.en: The simulated cap-and-trade system fixed total allowances and let each factory trade with other factories.
examples.zh: 模拟的「总量控制与交易制度」固定了配额总量，并允许各工厂互相交易。

examples.en: We compared the cap-and-trade system with a model that charged a fixed amount for each emission unit.
examples.zh: 我们把「总量控制与交易制度」和按每单位排放固定收费的模型作了比较。

collocations: compare a cap-and-trade system with a tax
model emissions under a cap-and-trade system

words.enDefinition: A limit on total emissions covered by a policy over a specified period.

examples.en: The emissions cap determined how many allowances the classroom market could issue for the first period.
examples.zh: 「排放总量上限」决定了课堂市场在第一个时期可以发放多少配额。

examples.en: Our group lowered the emissions cap in the simulation and recalculated the number of available permits.
examples.zh: 我们组在模拟中降低了「排放总量上限」，并重新计算可用的配额数量。

words.enDefinition: the market or auction price of a tradable emissions allowance

examples.en: The simulated permit price rose when several factories wanted to buy allowances in the same round.
examples.zh: 几家工厂都想在同一轮购买配额时，模拟中的「排放配额价格」上涨了。

examples.en: We compared the permit price with the cost of reducing one more unit in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们把「排放配额价格」与练习中再减排一个单位的成本作比较。

collocations: compare the permit price with abatement cost
report a change in the permit price

words.enDefinition: The first distribution of tradable emissions allowances before participants start trading them.

examples.en: The initial permit allocation gave two simulated factories different allowances before any permits changed hands.
examples.zh: 在任何配额交易发生前，「排放配额初始分配」给两家模拟工厂发放了不同数量的配额。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the initial permit allocation with the holdings after the first trading round.
examples.zh: 老师对比了「排放配额初始分配」和第一轮交易结束后的持有量。

words.enDefinition: A sale of emissions allowances to participants through competitive bidding.

examples.en: The classroom permit auction gave teams an opportunity to bid for the simulation's initial allowances.
examples.zh: 课堂「排放配额拍卖」给各队竞买模拟初始配额的机会。

examples.en: We compared revenue from the permit auction with revenue under free allocation in our exercise.
examples.zh: 我们对比了练习中「排放配额拍卖」和免费分配两种情形下的收入。

collocations: report revenue from a permit auction

words.enDefinition: Distributing emissions allowances to participants without charging them for the initial allocation.

examples.en: The example used free allocation of permits, but firms could still buy or sell them later.
examples.zh: 例题采用「免费分配排放配额」，之后企业仍可买卖所获配额。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how free allocation of permits affected the starting positions of the simulated factories.
examples.zh: 老师问，「免费分配排放配额」怎样影响各模拟工厂的初始条件。

collocations: compare free allocation of permits with auctions
model the effects of free allocation of permits

words.enDefinition: Saving unused emissions allowances for use in a later period when a trading program permits it.

examples.en: The simulation allowed permit banking, so unused allowances could be carried into the following period.
examples.zh: 模拟允许「配额结转」，因此未用完的配额可以带到下一期。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why permit banking might change the timing of reductions in a classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师问，「配额结转」为什么可能改变课堂模型中的减排时间。

collocations: compare scenarios with and without permit banking

words.enDefinition: The interval over which covered emissions are assessed against the allowances required by a program.

examples.en: The simulation measured factory releases throughout the emissions compliance period before checking the allowances held.
examples.zh: 模拟记录整个「排放合规期」内各工厂的排放情况，再核查它们持有的配额。

examples.en: Our worksheet compared two policies using the same length of emissions compliance period for both.
examples.zh: 练习表对两种政策采用相同的「排放合规期」长度进行比较。

collocations: report emissions for a compliance period

words.enDefinition: a tax on covered greenhouse gas emissions or on the carbon content of fuels under the stated policy design

examples.en: The case modelled a carbon tax based on the emissions from each simulated production run.
examples.zh: 案例对每轮模拟生产所产生的排放设置「碳税」模型。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how a carbon tax differed from setting the quantity of allowances in advance.
examples.zh: 老师问，征收「碳税」和预先设定配额数量有哪些区别。

collocations: estimate the effects of a carbon tax
compare a carbon tax with permit trading

words.enDefinition: A good whose use is nonrival and from which people are difficult to exclude.

examples.en: The example treated a warning reaching all nearby households at once as a public good.
examples.zh: 例题把能同时传达给附近各户的预警视为「公共物品」。

examples.en: We checked both characteristics before calling the shared information service a public good in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中将这项共享信息服务称为「公共物品」前，我们核查了它是否具备两项特征。

collocations: classify a service as a public good

words.enDefinition: The property that one user's consumption does not reduce what others can consume.

examples.en: The tutor illustrated nonrivalry with a notice that many people could read at the same time.
examples.zh: 老师用一则可供多人同时阅读的公告说明「非竞争性」。

examples.en: Our group questioned whether nonrivalry still held when the shared facility became crowded during the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们组讨论，课堂例题中的共享设施变得拥挤后，使用它是否仍有「非竞争性」。

collocations: an example of nonrivalry in use

words.enDefinition: the property of being costly or impractical to prevent particular people from benefiting from a good

examples.en: The example showed nonexcludability because the neighbourhood warning could reach households that had not contributed.
examples.zh: 社区预警也会传到没出资的家庭，例题以此说明「非排他性」。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed nonexcludability before asking why a provider might struggle to collect payments from users.
examples.zh: 老师先讲了「非排他性」，再问提供者为什么可能难以向使用者收费。

words.enDefinition: The property that one person's use reduces the amount or quality available for others.

examples.en: The example showed rivalry in consumption because one person taking a book left fewer for everyone else.
examples.zh: 有人取走一本书，给其他人留下的书就少一本，例题以此展示「消费竞争性」。

examples.en: We discussed how crowding might create rivalry in consumption at an otherwise quiet shared facility.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了拥挤如何在原本清静的共享设施中产生「消费竞争性」。

collocations: compare cases with different rivalry in consumption

words.enDefinition: The feasibility of preventing particular users from accessing a good or service.

examples.en: The classroom exercise used a ticketed stream to explain excludability for a service with many viewers.
examples.zh: 课堂练习用凭票观看的直播来说明一项有许多观看者的服务如何体现「排他性」。

examples.en: Our group considered excludability before classifying the two recreational facilities shown on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们组先考虑「排他性」，再把练习表上的两处休闲设施归类。

words.enDefinition: A good that users can be excluded from and whose consumption reduces availability for others.

examples.en: The class used a sandwich as a private good because it could be sold and consumed individually.
examples.zh: 全班用三明治举例说明「私人物品」，因为它可以卖给个人并被个人食用。

examples.en: We compared a private good sold at the kiosk with the information displayed outside for everyone.
examples.zh: 我们把售货亭出售的一种「私人物品」与外面供所有人查看的信息作了比较。

collocations: classify a product as a private good
contrast a private good with a public good

words.enDefinition: A good that can exclude users while being largely nonrival, at least below capacity.

examples.en: The exercise classified a members-only video stream as a club good while additional viewers caused no congestion.
examples.zh: 额外观看者不会造成拥挤时，练习把会员专享直播分类为「俱乐部物品」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether a crowded facility still behaved like a club good in the example.
examples.zh: 老师问，例题里的设施拥挤后是否仍表现得像一种「俱乐部物品」。

collocations: classify a service as a club good

words.enDefinition: A resource whose users are hard to exclude and whose use reduces what remains for others.

examples.en: The worksheet used a jointly accessible fishery as a common-pool resource in its simple model.
examples.zh: 练习表在简化模型中把各方都可进入的渔场用作「公共池资源」。

examples.en: The water source was a common-pool resource because access was difficult to limit and withdrawals depleted it.
examples.zh: 这处水源难以限制使用，取水也会减少储量，因此属于「公共池资源」。

collocations: model depletion of a common-pool resource

words.enDefinition: A resource with no effective rule limiting who may use or extract from it.

examples.en: The classroom model treated the fishery as an open access resource with no effective limit on entry.
examples.zh: 课堂模型把这个没有有效准入限制的渔场视为「开放使用资源」。

examples.en: We compared an open access resource with a pond that only designated households could use.
examples.zh: 我们比较了一项「开放使用资源」与只有指定家庭才能使用的一处池塘。

collocations: compare an open access resource with restricted access

words.enDefinition: An arrangement in which a defined group jointly holds and governs rights over a resource.

examples.en: The case described a common property regime under which a defined group shared rights to the pond.
examples.zh: 案例介绍了某项「共同产权制度」，在该制度下一个明确的群体共享池塘权利。

examples.en: Our tutor explained how a common property regime could set rules about who used the resource.
examples.zh: 老师解释了「共同产权制度」怎样规定谁有资格使用资源。

collocations: distinguish a common property regime from open access

words.enDefinition: Delay or crowding costs one additional user imposes on other users of a shared facility.

examples.en: The model showed a congestion externality when each extra car slowed the other cars on the route.
examples.zh: 每多一辆车都会让线路上其他车辆慢下来，模型展示了这种「拥挤外部性」。

examples.en: The group discussed a congestion externality at a small facility during the busiest part of the day.
examples.zh: 小组讨论了一处小型设施在一天中最忙时段产生的「拥挤外部性」。

collocations: a congestion externality on a shared route

words.enDefinition: Underfunding or underprovision that can result when users benefit from a good without contributing to it.

examples.en: The free-rider problem appeared when households could benefit from the warning service without paying for it.
examples.zh: 家庭不付费也能从预警服务中受益时，出现了「搭便车问题」。

examples.en: Our tutor introduced the free-rider problem before asking why voluntary payments fell short in the example.
examples.zh: 老师先介绍了「搭便车问题」，再问例题中的自愿付款为什么不足。

collocations: show the free-rider problem in a model

words.enDefinition: Overuse or depletion of a shared resource when individual users do not bear the full costs of their use.

examples.en: The exercise illustrated the tragedy of the commons when total withdrawals left the shared well nearly empty.
examples.zh: 取水总量使共享水井近乎干涸，练习借此展示了「公地悲剧」。

examples.en: We asked whether agreed access rules could prevent the tragedy of the commons in the classroom fishery.
examples.zh: 我们问，共同商定的使用规则能否防止课堂渔场出现「公地悲剧」。

collocations: explain the tragedy of the commons
illustrate the tragedy of the commons
a model of the tragedy of the commons

words.enDefinition: Use of a natural resource at a rate that depletes it or undermines its long-term renewal.

examples.en: The model predicted overexploitation when total fishing exceeded the rate at which the stock could recover.
examples.zh: 总捕捞量超过鱼群的恢复速度时，模型预测会出现「过度开发利用」。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed overexploitation after the simulation showed a smaller fish population in later rounds.
examples.zh: 模拟显示后续轮次鱼群数量减少之后，老师讨论了「过度开发利用」。

words.enDefinition: A fee charged for using a crowded road or facility to reflect delay or crowding costs.

examples.en: The classroom model added a congestion charge during the busiest hour on the simulated road.
examples.zh: 这个课堂模型在模拟道路最繁忙的一小时增加了「拥堵费」。

examples.en: We compared a congestion charge with a scenario in which every trip was priced the same.
examples.zh: 我们把实行「拥堵费」的情形与所有行程统一定价的情形作了比较。

collocations: estimate the effect of a congestion charge
compare trips before and after a congestion charge

words.enDefinition: A charge paid by those who use a particular facility or service.

examples.en: The example used a user fee to help pay for maintenance of a ticketed recreation facility.
examples.zh: 例题采用「使用者付费」，帮助承担凭票进入的休闲设施的维护成本。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how charging a user fee might change who attended the modelled events.
examples.zh: 老师问，实行「使用者付费」可能怎样改变模型中参加活动的人群。

collocations: fund a service with a user fee
analyse a change in a user fee

words.enDefinition: The arrangement of a good or service by government or another public body.

examples.en: The case compared public provision of neighbourhood lighting with relying on individual households to pay separately.
examples.zh: 案例对比由「公共部门提供」社区照明和依靠各家住户分别出资这两种情形。

examples.en: Our class asked whether public provision of the service also required staff to be public employees.
examples.zh: 全班问，由「公共部门提供」服务是否也要求工作人员必须受雇于公共部门。

collocations: compare public provision with private provision
fund public provision of a service

words.enDefinition: Coordination among people to pursue a common outcome that they cannot readily achieve alone.

examples.en: The classroom game showed how collective action could finance a service that benefited the whole group.
examples.zh: 课堂游戏展示了「集体行动」怎样为一项使全组受益的服务筹资。

examples.en: The tutor asked what made collective action harder when the number of participants grew.
examples.zh: 老师问，参加人数变多时，什么因素会让「集体行动」变难。

collocations: achieve a goal through collective action

words.enDefinition: A payment or other contribution made by choice to support a shared activity or good.

examples.en: The example modelled a voluntary contribution from each household towards a shared neighbourhood warning service.
examples.zh: 例题将各家庭为社区共享预警服务的「自愿出资」纳入模型。

examples.en: We compared the voluntary contribution in each round with the amount needed to provide the service.
examples.zh: 我们把各轮「自愿出资」与提供这项服务所需的金额作了比较。

collocations: collect voluntary contributions for a shared facility

words.enDefinition: The sum of the amounts individuals are willing to pay for a specified shared benefit.

examples.en: We added both households' valuations to obtain aggregate willingness to pay for the same extra warning device.
examples.zh: 我们把两户对同一台新增预警装置的估值相加，得到「总支付意愿」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared aggregate willingness to pay with the cost of installing one more public notice board.
examples.zh: 老师把「总支付意愿」与再装一块公共公告板的成本作了比较。

collocations: compare aggregate willingness to pay with the cost

words.enDefinition: Adding individuals' marginal willingness to pay at each shared quantity to obtain a public good's aggregate demand.

examples.en: We used vertical summation to add both users' values for the same extra unit of the public good.
examples.zh: 我们用「纵向加总」把两名使用者对同一个公共物品新增单位给出的估值相加。

examples.en: Our tutor drew vertical summation by adding the two values at each quantity on the graph.
examples.zh: 老师把图中各数量处的两个数值加起来，以说明「纵向加总」。

collocations: derive aggregate demand by vertical summation
illustrate vertical summation on a graph

words.enDefinition: At an interior efficient quantity of a pure public good, the sum of individual marginal benefits equals marginal cost.

examples.en: The tutor used the Samuelson condition to find the efficient amount of lighting in a classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师用「萨缪尔森条件」求课堂模型中的有效照明量。

examples.en: Our worksheet applied the Samuelson condition by comparing combined extra benefits with the cost of another unit.
examples.zh: 练习表把合计额外收益与再增加一个单位的成本比较，应用了「萨缪尔森条件」。

collocations: derive the Samuelson condition for a public good

words.enDefinition: Provision of a public good or service below the quantity that would maximize social net benefits.

examples.en: The model showed underprovision when households contributed too little to pay for the efficient number of lights.
examples.zh: 各家庭出资不足以支付有效数量的路灯时，模型出现了「供给不足」。

examples.en: Our class discussed underprovision after comparing private contributions with the benefits received by all households.
examples.zh: 全班比较个人出资和所有家庭所得收益后，讨论了「供给不足」。

collocations: identify underprovision of a public good

words.enDefinition: A rule limiting who may use a resource, when they may use it, or how much they may take.

examples.en: The case modelled an access restriction that limited the number of users at the shared water source.
examples.zh: 案例模拟一项「资源使用限制」，规定了这个共享水源的使用人数上限。

examples.en: Our tutor compared an access restriction with a situation where anyone could take water from the source.
examples.zh: 老师把实施「资源使用限制」的情形与任何人都可从该水源取水的情形作了比较。

collocations: study an access restriction for a shared resource

words.enDefinition: A limit on the quantity of a natural resource that may be taken during a period.

examples.en: The exercise set a harvest quota for the shared fishery to model a limit on total catches.
examples.zh: 练习为共享渔场设定「资源采收配额」，模拟对捕捞总量的限制。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the harvest quota with a system that limited how many people could enter.
examples.zh: 老师把「资源采收配额」与限制进入人数的制度作了比较。

collocations: compare a harvest quota with unrestricted access
model the effect of a harvest quota

words.enDefinition: A situation in which one party to an exchange has relevant information that another party lacks.

examples.en: The used bicycle example illustrated asymmetric information because sellers knew more about the condition than buyers.
examples.zh: 二手自行车例题说明了「信息不对称」，因为卖家比买家更了解自行车状况。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how asymmetric information might change the price buyers were prepared to offer.
examples.zh: 老师问，「信息不对称」可能怎样改变买家愿意给出的价格。

collocations: analyse the effects of asymmetric information

words.enDefinition: Lack of reliable information needed to make a fully informed economic decision.

examples.en: The case studied imperfect information when neither seller nor buyer knew how long the equipment would last.
examples.zh: 买卖双方都不知道设备还能用多久，案例用这一情形讨论了「不完全信息」。

examples.en: Our group discussed how imperfect information affected the range of prices considered in the example.
examples.zh: 我们组讨论了「不完全信息」怎样影响例题所考虑的价格范围。

words.enDefinition: Relevant facts about a participant or product that one party knows but the other cannot readily observe.

examples.en: The model treated previous repairs as hidden information because only the bicycle seller knew about them.
examples.zh: 只有自行车卖家知道此前的维修，模型将其视作「隐藏信息」。

examples.en: We discussed hidden information before asking whether a credible inspection report could improve the transaction.
examples.zh: 我们先讨论了「隐藏信息」，再问可信的检验报告能否改善交易结果。

collocations: respond to hidden information with screening

words.enDefinition: An action taken by one party that another party cannot directly observe or readily verify.

examples.en: The instructor described maintenance effort as a hidden action because the workshop owner could not observe it.
examples.zh: 讲师把维护投入视为「隐藏行动」，因为工场的所有者无法观察它。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked whether the reward would encourage more care when effort was a hidden action.
examples.zh: 练习表问，在投入属于「隐藏行动」时，奖励能否让人更认真。

collocations: an incentive problem involving hidden action

words.enDefinition: A change in who participates in a market or contract because private information influences their choices.

examples.en: The classroom case showed adverse selection when owners of better bicycles declined the price buyers offered.
examples.zh: 更优质自行车的车主拒绝买家报价时，课堂案例展示了「逆向选择」。

examples.en: We discussed adverse selection before comparing what buyers knew with what the sellers already knew.
examples.zh: 我们先讨论了「逆向选择」，再比较买家知道的情况和卖家原先知道的情况。

collocations: evidence of adverse selection in a market

words.enDefinition: A change in incentives or behavior when another party bears some consequences and cannot readily observe the behavior.

examples.en: The exercise considered moral hazard when repair costs were shared but daily care could not be monitored.
examples.zh: 练习考虑了分摊维修费用、又无法观察日常养护时可能出现的「道德风险」。

examples.en: Our tutor used moral hazard to discuss why coverage might change maintenance effort in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师用「道德风险」讨论为什么在课堂模型中，获得保障可能改变维护投入。

collocations: distinguish moral hazard from adverse selection

words.enDefinition: A market where buyers cannot distinguish quality reliably, so lower-quality goods may drive out higher-quality ones.

examples.en: The seminar used a market for lemons to explain how good bicycles could disappear from the listings.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「柠檬市场」解释优质自行车为什么可能从商品列表中消失。

examples.en: Our group asked whether independent inspections could change the outcome in the example market for lemons.
examples.zh: 我们组问，独立检验能否改变例题中「柠檬市场」的结果。

collocations: evidence of a market for lemons

words.enDefinition: Uncertainty about a product's actual quality at the time an exchange is being considered.

examples.en: Quality uncertainty made the hypothetical buyers unwilling to offer more for the best used equipment.
examples.zh: 由于「质量不确定性」，假设中的买家不愿为最好的二手设备出更高的价。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how a verified inspection might reduce quality uncertainty in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 老师问，经核实的检验结果可能怎样减少课堂例题中的「质量不确定性」。

collocations: model quality uncertainty in a secondhand market

words.enDefinition: an equilibrium of a signalling model in which different types choose the same observable action, so it does not distinguish them

examples.en: The model had a pooling equilibrium when both types of seller made the same observable offer.
examples.zh: 两种类型的卖家都给出相同的可观察报价时，模型形成「混同均衡」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what buyers could infer about quality under the proposed pooling equilibrium.
examples.zh: 老师问，在设想的「混同均衡」下，买家能对质量推断出什么。

collocations: compare a pooling equilibrium with a separating one

words.enDefinition: An equilibrium in which different types choose distinguishable actions that reveal information about them.

examples.en: The model showed a separating equilibrium because higher and lower quality sellers chose different offers.
examples.zh: 质量较高和较低的卖家给出不同报价，因此模型显示「分离均衡」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked which choices buyers could observe in the proposed separating equilibrium for used bicycles.
examples.zh: 练习表问，在假设的二手自行车「分离均衡」下，买家可以观察到哪些选择。

words.enDefinition: In a lemons model, progressive withdrawal of higher-quality sellers as expected quality and prices fall.

examples.en: The simulation showed market unraveling after the withdrawal of good bicycles lowered buyers' willingness to pay.
examples.zh: 优质自行车退出后，买家的支付意愿下降，模拟展示了由此发生的「市场瓦解」。

examples.en: Our class discussed whether independent quality checks would slow market unraveling in the practice model.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了独立质量检查能否减缓练习模型中的「市场瓦解」。

collocations: assess the risk of market unraveling

words.enDefinition: Providing relevant details to another party so that its market decisions are better informed.

examples.en: The model used information disclosure to show buyers the recorded condition of each secondhand bicycle.
examples.zh: 模型通过「信息披露」向买家展示每辆二手自行车的已记录车况。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether information disclosure changed both the price and the number of trades.
examples.zh: 老师问，「信息披露」是否同时改变了价格和交易数量。

collocations: assess the effect of information disclosure

words.enDefinition: An observable action or indicator that receivers have reason to trust as evidence of hidden information.

examples.en: The case treated independently verified test results as a credible signal about the condition of equipment.
examples.zh: 案例把经过独立核实的检测结果视为有关设备状况的「可信信号」。

examples.en: We discussed what made a credible signal costly for sellers whose products had significant defects.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了什么因素会使产品存在严重缺陷的卖家付出高代价才能发出「可信信号」。

collocations: a credible signal of product quality

words.enDefinition: Using an observable action that takes resources and is harder for some types to imitate.

examples.en: Our worksheet used costly signaling to explain why an inspection could distinguish two types of seller.
examples.zh: 练习表用「有成本的信号传递」解释为什么检验能够区分两类卖家。

examples.en: The tutor asked why costly signaling failed to separate the sellers when both could pass inspection cheaply.
examples.zh: 老师问，两类卖家都能以很低的成本通过检验时，「有成本的信号传递」为什么不能将他们区分开。

collocations: explain costly signaling in a used goods market

words.enDefinition: Observable actions by a better-informed party that convey information to a less-informed party.

examples.en: The used goods exercise modelled signaling when sellers provided verified inspection reports about their products.
examples.zh: 二手商品练习将卖家提供经核实的检验报告作为「信号传递」来建模。

examples.en: Our tutor distinguished signaling by sellers from screening initiated by buyers in the classroom case.
examples.zh: 老师区分了课堂案例中卖家进行的「信号传递」和买家发起的筛选。

words.enDefinition: Actions by a less-informed party to learn about or distinguish types that are privately known.

examples.en: The classroom buyers used screening when they asked a neutral inspector to assess the bicycles.
examples.zh: 课堂模型中的买家请中立检验员评估自行车，借此进行「筛选」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how screening would work if buyers could offer sellers two different contract options.
examples.zh: 老师问，如果买家能给卖家提供两种合同选择，「筛选」会如何发挥作用。

collocations: use screening to learn about quality

words.enDefinition: A test or choice arranged to reveal information about participants whose types are not directly observable.

examples.en: The exercise used a repair record check as a screening device in the modelled bicycle market.
examples.zh: 练习把维修记录核查用作自行车市场模型的一种「筛选机制」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked when a choice between two contracts might work as a screening device.
examples.zh: 老师问，让人从两种合同中选择何时能起到「筛选机制」的作用。

words.enDefinition: People sorting themselves among options according to preferences or information they privately hold.

examples.en: The model relied on self-selection because participants knew which of the two options suited them better.
examples.zh: 模型依靠「自我选择」，因为参加者知道两个选项哪个更适合自己。

examples.en: We discussed how self-selection could reveal differences that the organiser could not observe directly.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「自我选择」如何揭示组织者无法直接观察到的差异。

words.enDefinition: A set of contracts offered together so participants can choose terms that suit their own circumstances.

examples.en: The model offered a menu of contracts that differed in their upfront fees and repair coverage.
examples.zh: 模型提供一套「合同选项组合」，各选项的前期费用与维修保障范围不同。

examples.en: The tutor asked why one menu of contracts might attract people with different expected usage levels.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么一套「合同选项组合」可能吸引预期使用量各不相同的人。

collocations: choose from a menu of contracts

words.enDefinition: Independent verification that a product or provider meets a stated standard.

examples.en: The market example used third-party certification to show buyers whether the equipment met an agreed standard.
examples.zh: 市场例题用「第三方认证」向买家表明设备是否符合商定标准。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how third-party certification might change buyers' confidence in the quality of listed bicycles.
examples.zh: 老师问，「第三方认证」可能怎样改变买家对上架自行车质量的信心。

collocations: use third-party certification as a signal

words.enDefinition: An arrangement in which past behaviour affects trust and future transactions, giving participants incentives to maintain quality.

examples.en: The case included a reputation mechanism in which past transactions affected how much buyers trusted each seller.
examples.zh: 案例包含一种「声誉机制」，其中过去的交易会影响买家对各卖家的信任。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the reputation mechanism still mattered when sellers expected only one transaction.
examples.zh: 老师问，当卖家预计只会发生一次交易时，「声誉机制」是否仍然重要。

collocations: a reputation mechanism based on reviews

words.enDefinition: A warranty that conveys quality information when reliable producers expect lower costs from offering it.

examples.en: The exercise analysed a warranty as a quality signal because defects would cost the seller money later.
examples.zh: 缺陷会让卖家之后承担费用，练习据此分析了「作为质量信号的质保」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked when a warranty as a quality signal might be convincing to buyers.
examples.zh: 老师问，「作为质量信号的质保」在什么情况下可能令买家信服。

collocations: offer a warranty as a quality signal
interpret a warranty as a quality signal
study a warranty as a quality signal

words.enDefinition: A conflict that arises when someone acting for another party has different incentives and their actions are hard to observe.

examples.en: The case illustrated a principal-agent problem because the owner and the contractor valued extra effort differently.
examples.zh: 所有者与承包方对额外投入的重视程度不同，案例以此说明「委托代理问题」。

examples.en: Our tutor explained how limited information about effort shaped the principal-agent problem in the exercise.
examples.zh: 老师解释了关于努力程度的信息有限，如何影响练习中的「委托代理问题」。

collocations: address a principal-agent problem with incentives

words.enDefinition: Resources spent observing or verifying how another party performs its responsibilities.

examples.en: The worksheet included a monitoring cost for the time spent checking whether the agreed work was complete.
examples.zh: 练习表把检查约定工作是否完成所花时间计入一项「监督成本」。

examples.en: We compared the monitoring cost with the benefit of avoiding errors in the hypothetical arrangement.
examples.zh: 我们把「监督成本」与假设安排中因避免错误而获得的收益作了比较。

collocations: compare a monitoring cost with expected benefits

words.enDefinition: A property of rules or contracts under which participants find the desired actions to be in their own interest.

examples.en: Our worksheet tested incentive compatibility by asking which option each type of participant would actually choose.
examples.zh: 练习表通过询问各类型参加者实际会选择什么选项，检验「激励相容性」。

examples.en: The tutor discussed incentive compatibility after changing the reward attached to one of the available options.
examples.zh: 老师调整了其中一个可选项的奖励后，讨论了「激励相容性」。

words.enDefinition: A contract linking a party's rewards to outcomes or measures intended to encourage desired behaviour.

examples.en: The simulated workshop used an incentive contract linking part of the payment to verified work quality.
examples.zh: 模拟工场用「激励合同」将部分报酬与经核实的工作质量挂钩。

examples.en: The class discussed whether the incentive contract rewarded outcomes that the contractor could actually influence.
examples.zh: 全班讨论这份「激励合同」所奖励的成果是否确实在承包方的影响范围内。

words.enDefinition: Combining potential losses across participants so that individual losses are shared by the group.

examples.en: The model illustrated risk pooling by sharing the cost of unexpected repairs across several participating workshops.
examples.zh: 模型将意外维修成本分摊给几家参加的工场，以说明「风险共担」。

examples.en: Our tutor used risk pooling to explain why average costs could be more predictable than individual costs.
examples.zh: 老师用「风险共担」解释为什么平均成本可能比个人成本更可预测。

words.enDefinition: A feedback process in which rising prices drive out lower-risk members, raising average costs and prices again.

examples.en: The classroom model showed an adverse selection spiral after lower-risk members left the hypothetical coverage pool.
examples.zh: 较低风险的成员离开假设的保障池后，课堂模型显示出现了「逆向选择螺旋」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked what assumptions made an adverse selection spiral possible in this simplified example.
examples.zh: 老师问，哪些假设使这个简化例题可能出现「逆向选择螺旋」。

collocations: test assumptions about an adverse selection spiral

words.enDefinition: Setting later premiums or contributions partly according to past reported losses or claims.

examples.en: The hypothetical plan used experience rating, so past repair claims affected the prices shown for later periods.
examples.zh: 假设计划采用「按历史赔付情况定价」，因此历史维修索赔影响后续期间的价格。

examples.en: Our class compared experience rating with a simple model where each group paid the same price.
examples.zh: 全班把「按历史赔付情况定价」与各组支付相同价格的简单模型作了比较。

collocations: discuss incentive effects of experience rating

words.enDefinition: Checking evidence to establish whether product or service quality matches the information provided.

examples.en: The model included the cost of quality verification when buyers requested an independent condition check.
examples.zh: 买家要求独立检查设备状况时，模型计入了「质量核验」成本。

examples.en: Our group discussed how better quality verification could increase trade in the example used goods market.
examples.zh: 我们组讨论了更完善的「质量核验」可能怎样增加例题中二手商品市场的成交量。

words.enDefinition: How the economic burden of a tax is divided among the people affected by it.

examples.en: The class analysed tax incidence by tracking changes in both the buyer price and the seller's receipts.
examples.zh: 全班通过跟踪买方价格和卖方实收金额的变化来分析「税负归宿」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why tax incidence could differ from the rule about who forwarded payments to the government.
examples.zh: 老师问，「税负归宿」为什么可能与谁负责向政府缴款的规定不同。

collocations: explain tax incidence in a supply and demand model

words.enDefinition: The assignment of the legal responsibility for a tax to a particular party.

examples.en: The worksheet assigned statutory incidence to sellers even though buyers bore part of the economic burden.
examples.zh: 虽然买方也承担部分经济负担，练习表仍把「法定税负归属」指定在卖方一侧。

examples.en: We changed the statutory incidence in the classroom model before comparing the resulting prices.
examples.zh: 我们先改变课堂模型中的「法定税负归属」，再比较变动后的价格。

collocations: compare statutory incidence with economic incidence
change the statutory incidence of a tax

words.enDefinition: The economic cost borne by an individual or group as a result of a tax.

examples.en: The worksheet showed that the tax burden was shared between customers and sellers in the market.
examples.zh: 练习表显示，市场里的顾客和卖方共同承担「税收负担」。

examples.en: We compared the tax burden in two examples with different responses to a price increase.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个对涨价反应不同的例题中的「税收负担」。

words.enDefinition: The part of a tax borne by buyers, measured per unit by their price increase in the standard model.

examples.en: We calculated the buyer tax burden as the difference between the prices customers paid before and after taxation.
examples.zh: 我们以征税前后顾客支付价格的差额计算「买方税负」。

examples.en: With the same supply curve, the buyer tax burden was larger where demand was less elastic.
examples.zh: 在供给曲线相同的情况下，需求弹性较小的情形下「买方税负」更大。

collocations: compare the buyer tax burden across markets
explain differences in the buyer tax burden

words.enDefinition: The part of a tax borne by sellers, measured per unit by the reduction in the price they retain.

examples.en: The seller tax burden reflected the drop in the amount each seller kept per sale.
examples.zh: 「卖方税负」反映了卖家从每笔销售中留存金额的下降。

examples.en: Our tutor found the seller tax burden by comparing the seller's net price with the original price.
examples.zh: 老师比较卖方实收净价与原价，求出了「卖方税负」。

collocations: compare the seller tax burden across markets
identify the seller tax burden on a graph

words.enDefinition: The difference a tax creates between the price buyers pay and the price sellers retain.

examples.en: The diagram showed a tax wedge between what customers paid and what sellers kept per sale.
examples.zh: 图中显示，顾客支付金额与卖家从每笔销售留存的金额之间出现了「税楔」。

examples.en: We labelled the tax wedge before calculating how the buyers and sellers shared the modelled tax.
examples.zh: 计算买卖双方如何分担模型中的税之前，我们先标出了「税楔」。

collocations: show the tax wedge between the two prices

words.enDefinition: A tax charging a fixed amount for each unit of a good sold or activity undertaken.

examples.en: The classroom model used a per-unit tax that charged the same amount for every basket sold.
examples.zh: 课堂模型采用「单位商品定额税」，每卖出一个篮子都征收相同金额。

examples.en: We drew the price difference created by a per-unit tax in the simple market model.
examples.zh: 我们画出了「单位商品定额税」在简单市场模型中造成的价格差。

collocations: compare a per-unit tax with a percentage tax

words.enDefinition: A tax calculated as a percentage of a good's value or a transaction price.

examples.en: The worksheet used an ad valorem tax, so the amount owed depended on the item's value.
examples.zh: 练习表采用「从价税」，因此税额取决于商品价值。

examples.en: Our tutor compared an ad valorem tax with charging a fixed amount for each unit sold.
examples.zh: 老师把「从价税」与每卖出一个单位征收固定金额的方式作了比较。

collocations: compare an ad valorem tax with a per-unit tax

words.enDefinition: A payment of a specified amount for each qualifying unit produced, bought, or sold.

examples.en: The classroom example paid a per-unit subsidy for every additional basket sold under the scheme.
examples.zh: 在课堂例题中，该计划对每多售出的一个篮子提供「单位商品定额补贴」。

examples.en: We compared the per-unit subsidy with a fixed payment that did not depend on quantity sold.
examples.zh: 我们把「单位商品定额补贴」与不随销量变化的固定付款作了比较。

collocations: calculate the cost of a per-unit subsidy

words.enDefinition: The division of the economic benefits of a subsidy across the groups it affects.

examples.en: The worksheet used subsidy incidence to show how buyers and sellers could both gain from the payment.
examples.zh: 练习表用「补贴归宿」展示买卖双方怎样都可能从这笔款项中受益。

examples.en: Our tutor analysed subsidy incidence after calculating changes in buyer and seller prices under the policy.
examples.zh: 老师计算了政策下买方和卖方价格的变动，再分析「补贴归宿」。

collocations: explain subsidy incidence with a diagram

words.enDefinition: A stated price that includes the tax payable on the transaction.

examples.en: The exercise displayed the tax-inclusive price paid by customers above the net amount received by sellers.
examples.zh: 练习把顾客支付的「含税价格」列在卖家收到的净额上方。

examples.en: We compared the tax-inclusive price in the diagram with what buyers paid before the tax was introduced.
examples.zh: 我们比较了图中的「含税价格」与征税前买家支付的价格。

collocations: compare the tax-inclusive price with the pre-tax amount

words.enDefinition: The amount stated for a good or service before the applicable tax is added.

examples.en: In the exercise, the tax-exclusive price was shown below the full amount paid by the buyer.
examples.zh: 练习中的「不含税价格」列在买方支付总额下方。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the tax-exclusive price with the total to check how much tax was charged.
examples.zh: 老师比较「不含税价格」与总额，核对加收了多少税。

collocations: calculate tax from a tax-exclusive price
compare the tax-exclusive price with the final amount

words.enDefinition: The change in a buyer's price relative to the change in the tax per unit.

examples.en: We divided the change in the buyer price by the tax change to find the tax pass-through rate.
examples.zh: 我们用买方价格变动除以税额变动，求得「税收转嫁率」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the tax pass-through rate in two fictional markets with different demand responses.
examples.zh: 老师比较了两个需求反应不同的虚构市场各自的「税收转嫁率」。

words.enDefinition: A case in which less than the full amount of a tax change reaches buyers through price changes.

examples.en: The worksheet showed incomplete tax pass-through because the buyer price rose by less than the new tax.
examples.zh: 买方价格的涨幅小于新税额，练习表据此展示了「税收不完全转嫁」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared incomplete tax pass-through with a case where the buyer's price rose by the entire tax.
examples.zh: 老师把「税收不完全转嫁」与买方价格涨幅等于全部税额的例题作了比较。

collocations: explain incomplete tax pass-through with a graph

words.enDefinition: A case in which the buyer's price changes by exactly the change in the tax per unit.

examples.en: The simulation showed full tax pass-through when the buyer price increased by exactly the tax amount.
examples.zh: 买方价格涨幅恰好等于税额时，模拟显示「税收完全转嫁」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which supply conditions could produce full tax pass-through in the simple classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师问，在简单课堂模型中，哪些供给条件可能产生「税收完全转嫁」。

collocations: compare full tax pass-through with incomplete pass-through

words.enDefinition: A case in which the buyer's price changes by more than the change in tax per unit.

examples.en: The imperfectly competitive model showed tax overshifting when the buyer price rose more than the tax amount.
examples.zh: 在不完全竞争模型中，买方价格的涨幅超过税额，出现了「税收超额转嫁」。

examples.en: Our tutor checked the tax amount and buyer price change before describing the result as tax overshifting.
examples.zh: 老师核对了税额与买方价格的变化，才将结果描述为「税收超额转嫁」。

collocations: test whether the result indicates tax overshifting

words.enDefinition: Money received by a government or other public authority through taxes.

examples.en: We calculated tax revenue by multiplying the amount per unit by the quantity sold after taxation.
examples.zh: 我们把单位税额乘以征税后的销量，计算出「税收收入」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why higher tax revenue did not necessarily mean higher overall welfare in the model.
examples.zh: 老师问，为什么模型中较高的「税收收入」并不一定意味着较高的总体福利。

collocations: compare tax revenue under two policies
show tax revenue on a diagram

words.enDefinition: the reduction in overall surplus caused by a tax changing behaviour, after also counting the revenue collected, relative to the specified baseline

examples.en: The graph showed tax-induced deadweight loss from trades that would have benefited buyers and sellers before taxation.
examples.zh: 在这个模型中，征税使原本对双方有利的交易不再发生。图中展示了「税收造成的无谓损失」。

examples.en: Our tutor separated tax-induced deadweight loss from the revenue collected on transactions that still took place.
examples.zh: 老师把「税收造成的无谓损失」与仍发生的交易所产生的税收分开。

collocations: compare tax-induced deadweight loss across cases

words.enDefinition: The additional deadweight loss per additional unit of tax revenue raised by a small tax increase.

examples.en: The worksheet estimated marginal excess burden by comparing the extra welfare loss with the extra revenue raised.
examples.zh: 练习表把额外福利损失与新增税收收入比较，估算「边际超额负担」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared marginal excess burden for two small changes in the course's tax model.
examples.zh: 老师比较了课程税收模型中两项小幅调整的「边际超额负担」。

collocations: compare the marginal excess burden of two taxes

words.enDefinition: a tax payment fixed independently of the taxpayer's choices in the model

examples.en: The classroom model used a lump-sum tax that was unchanged when a household altered its purchases.
examples.zh: 课堂模型采用「定额总付税」，即使家庭改变购买选择，税额也不变。

examples.en: We compared a lump-sum tax with a charge applied to each transaction in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们把「定额总付税」与练习中对每笔交易征收的税作了比较。

collocations: compare a lump-sum tax with a per-unit tax
raise revenue through a lump-sum tax

words.enDefinition: A tax that changes relative prices or incentives and can therefore alter economic decisions.

examples.en: The worksheet showed a distortionary tax changing which of two goods consumers chose in the model.
examples.zh: 练习表展示了「扭曲性税收」怎样改变模型中消费者在两种商品之间的选择。

examples.en: Our tutor compared a distortionary tax with a payment that did not depend on individual behaviour.
examples.zh: 老师把「扭曲性税收」与一项不取决于个人行为的缴款作了比较。

collocations: analyse responses to a distortionary tax
compare a distortionary tax with a fixed levy

words.enDefinition: A reform designed to keep government revenue unchanged relative to a specified baseline.

examples.en: The classroom case designed a revenue-neutral reform but found different households would pay different amounts afterward.
examples.zh: 课堂案例设计了「税收收入中性的改革」，但发现改革后各家庭的缴款额会发生不同变化。

examples.en: We compared receipts before and after the revenue-neutral reform to check the total in the model.
examples.zh: 我们对比「税收收入中性的改革」前后的收入，以核查模型中的合计。

collocations: compare two options for revenue-neutral reform
test assumptions in a revenue-neutral reform

words.enDefinition: The amount the public authority pays to fund a subsidy in the scenario being studied.

examples.en: We found the subsidy cost by multiplying the payment per unit by the quantity receiving it.
examples.zh: 我们把单位补贴额乘以获得补贴的数量，求出了「补贴财政支出」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared subsidy cost with changes in social benefits and other costs in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师将「补贴财政支出」与课堂模型中社会收益和其他成本的变化作了比较。

collocations: estimate the subsidy cost at the new quantity

words.enDefinition: An increase in overall welfare relative to a baseline once relevant benefits and costs are included.

examples.en: The exercise found a net welfare gain after comparing reduced noise damage with the cost of abatement.
examples.zh: 练习把减少的噪声损害和治理成本比较后，发现存在「净福利增益」。

examples.en: We calculated the net welfare gain against the baseline chosen for the classroom policy comparison.
examples.zh: 我们按课堂政策对比中选定的基准计算了「净福利增益」。

collocations: compare net welfare gains across policies

words.enDefinition: A change making at least one person better off without making anyone worse off.

examples.en: The trade represented a Pareto improvement because one participant gained and nobody in the model lost.
examples.zh: 因为有一位参与者获益且模型中无人受损，这笔交易构成「帕累托改进」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether a positive total gain alone proved a Pareto improvement for the group.
examples.zh: 老师问，总增益为正本身是否足以证明这项变化对小组构成「帕累托改进」。

words.enDefinition: A situation in which improving a specified measure of fairness can reduce overall economic efficiency, or vice versa.

examples.en: The seminar explored an equity-efficiency trade-off by comparing total welfare with the distribution of benefits.
examples.zh: 研讨课将总体福利与收益的分布作比较，探讨「公平与效率的权衡」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the two policy options actually involved an equity-efficiency trade-off in this model.
examples.zh: 老师问，在这个模型中，两种政策选项是否真的涉及「公平与效率的权衡」。

collocations: discuss the equity-efficiency trade-off in a model

words.enDefinition: How a policy's benefits or costs differ among people or groups.

examples.en: The report described the distributional impact of the fee by separating frequent users from occasional users.
examples.zh: 报告把常用者和偶尔使用者分开，说明收费的「分配影响」。

examples.en: We studied distributional impact even though the two options had the same total net benefit.
examples.zh: 尽管这两个选项具有同样的总净收益，我们仍研究了「分配影响」。

collocations: compare the distributional impacts of two policies

words.enDefinition: Factors applied to gains and losses of different groups to reflect an explicit welfare judgment.

examples.en: The worksheet used distributional weights to illustrate how equal payments could receive different importance in welfare analysis.
examples.zh: 练习表用「分配权重」说明，在福利分析里金额相同的付款怎样可能具有不同重要性。

examples.en: We recalculated the policy comparison using different distributional weights for the two hypothetical groups.
examples.zh: 我们对两个假设群体采用不同的「分配权重」，重新计算政策对比结果。

collocations: test the sensitivity to distributional weights

words.enDefinition: A situation in which a public intervention produces inefficient outcomes because of limitations such as information or incentives.

examples.en: The case illustrated government failure when the rule cost more to administer than the benefits it created.
examples.zh: 案例中的规定实施成本高于所产生的收益，体现了「政府失灵」。

examples.en: The class discussed government failure after finding that the policy missed the households it was intended to reach.
examples.zh: 发现政策未惠及目标家庭后，全班讨论了「政府失灵」。

collocations: explain a source of government failure
compare government failure with market failure

words.enDefinition: A situation in which regulation is unduly influenced to serve regulated or other special interests.

examples.en: The fictional case examined regulatory capture after the agency consistently prioritised the interests of regulated firms.
examples.zh: 虚构案例分析了「监管俘获」，其中机构一贯将受监管企业的利益放在优先位置。

examples.en: Our tutor asked how regulatory capture might change which costs were counted in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 老师问，「监管俘获」可能怎样改变课堂模型将哪些成本纳入计算。

collocations: identify a risk of regulatory capture
discuss the effects of regulatory capture

words.enDefinition: The estimated outcome that would have occurred without the policy or under a specified alternative.

examples.en: Our group defined a policy counterfactual before estimating the reduction in traffic from the trial fee.
examples.zh: 我们组先设定「政策反事实情景」，再估计试验性收费减少了多少车流。

examples.en: The tutor showed how choosing a different policy counterfactual changed the apparent benefits of the intervention.
examples.zh: 老师展示了选择不同的「政策反事实情景」如何改变干预措施所显示的收益。

collocations: test sensitivity to the policy counterfactual

words.enDefinition: Total benefits divided by total costs, using comparable valuations and discounting when the analysis spans time.

examples.en: We calculated the benefit-cost ratio for the classroom proposal after expressing costs and benefits on the same basis.
examples.zh: 在统一成本与收益的计量口径后，我们计算了课堂方案的「收益成本比」。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the benefit-cost ratio with net benefits, calculated by subtracting estimated costs from benefits.
examples.zh: 老师把「收益成本比」与收益扣减估算成本后得到的净收益作了比较。

collocations: compare the benefit-cost ratios of two projects

words.enDefinition: Comparing the benefits and costs of an action for society, including effects outside the immediate transaction.

examples.en: The class used social cost-benefit analysis to compare a quieter delivery schedule with the original one.
examples.zh: 全班用「社会成本收益分析」比较降噪后的配送时段与原来的安排。

examples.en: Our tutor included effects on nearby residents in the social cost-benefit analysis of the classroom proposal.
examples.zh: 老师在课堂方案的「社会成本收益分析」中计入了对附近居民的影响。

collocations: document assumptions in a social cost-benefit analysis
